findings.title: Bounds sync-back uploads positions only, so reflect/soft velocity changes never reach the GPU
findings.description:
`apply_bounds_policy()` is passed both `positions` and `velocities`, but the only sync-back path is `notify_positions_modified()` → `upload_positions()`. Assuming REFLECT and SOFT mutate the velocities they are handed, the GPU state keeps the pre-bounds velocity. A reflected agent would then head back out of bounds every tick and be re-clamped on the host, pinning it to the wall.

- **Plan requirement unmet:** the plan entry assigns "bounds policy (sync-back … for wrap/reflect/soft)" to this slice; only WRAP is covered correctly.
- **Not caught by the tests:** A4 checks only "finite, in-bounds" on downloaded arrays, and test 7 covers WRAP only.
- **Fix:** sync velocities as well for REFLECT/SOFT (for example a single `notify_state_modified(positions, velocities)`), and add a reflect test asserting the velocity sign after the bounce.
- **Doc mismatch:** the `step()` snippet at lines 185-191 omits the `notify_positions_modified()` call the prose describes.

findings.title: Spawn/despawn sync is under-specified and conflicts with the dirty-positions mechanism
findings.description:
The plan assigns "spawn/despawn (re-upload changed agent state)" to this slice. Four gaps leave it unmet:

- **Source of truth:** on the GPU path nothing in the design writes tick results back to `entity_manager.state`. `sync_from_entity_manager()` would then re-upload stale CPU state, resetting every agent to its last-synced position on any spawn. The design must say whether results are written back each tick or how the sync merges new agents with live GPU state.
- **Field capacity:** `setup_from_server()` sizes fields from `entity_manager.count` at startup. The design does not say how a larger count fits (pre-allocate to a maximum capacity, or reallocate). Line 382 itself notes a second `qd.init()` is undefined behaviour, so reallocation is not free.
- **Stale pending upload:** with a non-OPEN policy, `_pending_positions` from the previous tick has the old count. `sync_from_entity_manager()` runs first, then `step()` uploads the stale array over the fresh state. The sync must clear the dirty flag.
- **Change detection:** comparing counts misses a despawn plus spawn in the same tick. A mutation flag or version counter set by the spawn/despawn operations is more reliable, and avoids putting "last tick" bookkeeping on `EntityManager`.

Test 6 only asserts "does not raise", which would pass with all four defects present.

findings.title: `_select_arch()` selects by OS, not by GPU detection, contradicting A7 and the plan
findings.description:
The plan entry and A7 say "if neither is detected it warns and falls back to `qd.cpu`". The function returns `qd.cuda` for any Linux host and `qd.metal` for any Darwin host; the fallback fires only on other platforms.

- **Consequence:** per line 382, a Linux host without a CUDA driver makes `qd.init()` raise and the server exit. Because `quadrants` is the default, every CUDA-less Linux box or CI runner fails to start on the default config.
- **Fix:** either catch the specific init failure and retry on `qd.cpu` with the WARNING, or probe availability before selecting. Reword the log message, which currently claims "No supported GPU detected" on a path that never checks.
- **Missing test:** A7 has no corresponding test in §Testing.
- **Minor inconsistency:** line 252 says `arch` returns `"cuda"` or `"metal"`; line 224 includes `"cpu"`.

findings.title: Tier 2 gate configuration is unspecified and the default may not meet it
findings.description:
The NFR is correctly restated (≥60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA, A6). The gate test does not state `subdivision_factor`, bounds policy or workload density.

- **Default S=1:** the plan records 38 TPS at N=50k for slice 145, with the target reached only after slices 148 and 149 (149 used S=3). The design defaults to `subdivision_factor: 1`, so the default production config may miss the gate.
- **Added transfers:** production adds per-tick velocity and profile-index downloads, plus a position upload on non-OPEN policies. Slice 145's design point was a single position download.
- **Fix:** pin the gate's S, bounds policy and density, and either default S to the validated value or state that Tier 2 requires S=3.

findings.title: Production-to-bench dependency is only partly removed
findings.description:
Moving `GpuAgentState` to `migratory.gpu` is the right direction. But `GpuSimulationDriver.step()` also calls `build_spatial_hash`, `fused_force_integrate_kernel` and `TickResult.from_quadrants_fields`, and `_select_arch()` is "updated from the bench backend version". The design does not say where these live.

- **Kernels:** if they remain under `bench/backends/`, `migratory_server` still imports from the bench harness, which is the hidden dependency line 383 claims to eliminate. State their module, and move them to `migratory.gpu` if needed.
- **`_select_arch()`:** say whether it is shared (which changes bench behaviour, contrary to the out-of-scope statement) or a production-only copy.
- **Self-contradiction:** the table lists `quadrants_fused_backend.py` as changed, then line 301 says it is not.

findings.title: Test plan and walkthrough contradict the design
findings.description:
- **Line 307:** "All tests are CPU-only" is followed by "skip if GPU not available" and "tests run on Metal/CUDA". State which substrate CI uses; `qd.cpu` would let tests 5-8 run everywhere.
- **Process isolation:** line 382 requires subprocess isolation because a second `qd.init()` is undefined, but tests 5-8 each call `setup()` with no isolation strategy.
- **Coverage of A4:** it claims all four bounds policies; only WRAP has a test.
- **Stale walkthrough:** "CPU default (no GPU)" (lines 358-362) says removing the `compute:` block yields the CPU path, but the default is `quadrants`. Step 5 at line 351 says "Restore `backend: cpu`" for the same reason.

findings.title: Precision and Metal claims diverge from the slice plan's record
findings.description: The design says f32 GPU fields were "established in slices 143–145". The plan's substrate notes say slice 145 uses f64 `_ti` kernels on CUDA and lists "Metal not targeted" for 145. A2's golden-path demo is on Metal, so confirm the fused kernel actually runs there and state the precision per arch. Otherwise A2 rests on an unverified substrate.

findings.title: Scope, boundaries and proportionality match the plan entry
findings.description: The config block, the `GpuSimulationDriver` owning lifecycle, the unchanged world-server call site and preserved `TickResult` contract (A3), and the host-side bounds choice over a GPU kernel all match the plan entry. Out-of-scope items align with plan 300 and Future Work. The mechanism count fits effort 3; nothing needs cutting.

findings.title: Startup and fatal-GPU failure handling is explicit
findings.description: Invalid config fails at parse time before the port binds. `qd.init()` and allocation failures propagate and exit at startup. A mid-session GPU failure is declared process-fatal with restart as the recovery unit. `finalize()` is safe after a partial setup.
